text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Friday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Lithuanian lawmakers rejected the recommendation of the Homeland Union faction to restrict the government from taking decisions on key economic and financial issues during its remaining term.

- The Centre Union, which came third in the recent elections, will support one of the leaders of the Homeland Union party Gediminas Vagnorius for the post of prime minister if he is suggested by President Algirdas Brazauskas but under 'certain circumstances'.
- Sweden will provide 1.5 billion litas worth technical aid until 1998 to help Lithuania's integration to the European Union (EU).
- Lithuania's foreign debt was $828.4 milion at the beginning of October.

- Brazauskas has invited for lunch the leaders of the five parties which got into parliament after the elections. Homeland Union leader Vytautas Landsbergis said it was a waste of time as the formation of the new government should be carried out between the president and the future coalition of the Homeland Union and the Christian Democrats.
- One more Lithuanian, Jonas Stelmokas, might be stripped of his U.S. citizenship for alleged participatiaon in the Holocaust.
- Negotiations between Lithuania and Latvia concerning their disputed sea border will have to start from the very beginning after Brazauskas renounced all previous agreements on Wednesday.
- The government refused to issue guarantees for credits to the energy sector and suggested to arrange a new bid to buy heating oil.
- The Centre Union will work with the right-wing coalition said its leader Romualdas Ozolas.

- The government has so far refused to back the energy ministry's suggestion to sell a part of the state-owned Klaipedos Nafta shares to Russian oil company Jukos. Some 51 percent of the firm is owned by the state and 49 percent by Lancaster Steel Co Inc. Both sides agreed earlier to sell five percent each in exchange for a Jukos guarantee to export three million tonnes of oil products via the terminal.
